attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post. The quote that follows is his remark to Manjoo, also his own words.

semantics.note: A plain present-tense description of ChatGPT as it was at release. The normalised wording keeps the scope and adds nothing.

contract.note: The plain reading (simple prompts or rewordings readily produce errors) is ordinary and fair. Limiting the period to release through the post date fits the context. No error rate is required.

evidence.note: Dated Dec 21 transcripts of the original ChatGPT. It makes false, self-contradicting claims on simple arithmetic parity questions, including when the question is asked neutrally.

Peer-reviewed study whose tests were run Dec 14, inside the period. Rewording the same question gave opposite advice. That shows instability, though a moral disagreement is weaker evidence than a factual error.
Contemporary preprint praising selected academic answers. It shows competence on some tasks but does not show robustness to simple prompts, so it does not meet the contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: Independent tests dated inside the period show repeated mistakes and inconsistencies on simple prompts without elaborate manipulation (e1, e2). The favourable preprint (e3) does not show broad robustness. The support condition is met under a fair plain reading.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, the first of his 'seven dark predictions' in his own post.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will' prediction with no deadline. The normalised wording keeps 'like its predecessors' and 'reckless and hard to control'.

contract.note: Reading the metaphor as recurring unwanted outputs despite constraints is ordinary and fits the surrounding text on control and guardrails. The result does depend on counting adversarial jailbreaks as 'hard to control', a reading the speaker did not spell out but that is reasonable.

evidence.note: Independent systematic jailbreak evaluation of released GPT-4 (data collected Apr–May 2023). It documents repeated harmful outputs despite safeguards. Qualification: plain requests rarely got harmful answers.

reviews.rationale: The early-resolution rule is met by a dated, independent, systematic evaluation showing recurring safety-control failures in released GPT-4. The study's own caveats (good behaviour on unmodified requests; some attacks weaker than on GPT-3.5) qualify how bad the failures were, but persistence is what the claim predicts. The result rests on the jailbreak reading of 'hard to control'.
